From the smoker

The three trays people cross the East River for

Everything is smoked in-house and sliced to order, Kansas City style — heavy bark, a real smoke ring, sauce on the side if you want it.

The signature

Brisket Burnt Ends

The point of the brisket, cubed, re-rubbed and smoked again until the bark turns to candy. “Thick with bark yet tender on the inside — an excellent representation of what Kansas City-style BBQ is all about.” — The Infatuation. They sell out most days.

$23 / ½ lb
Sliced to order

Beef Brisket

Low and slow until it bends over the knife. Pitmaster Josh Bowen's crew took “Brisket King of NYC” honors — this is the cut that built the reputation.

$22 / ½ lb
Dry-rubbed

Ribs & Pulled Pork

Rosy, glazed spare ribs with a clean bite — no fall-off-the-bone shortcuts — next to shoulder pulled by hand. Build a mixed tray by the pound.

$23 / ½ slab

Catering & group orders

The office lunch that makes you a hero

Barbecue is built for a crowd — it travels well, holds its heat, and nobody ever complains. Order by the pound and let the table do the rest.

  • By the pound: burnt ends, brisket, pulled pork, pastrami, pork belly, rib tips
  • Whole slabs & whole chickens for the center of the table
  • Sides by the tray: mac and cheese, baked beans, collards, slaw, cornbread
  • Game days, office lunches, backyard parties — call ahead and it's hot when you arrive

The backyard

A beer garden hiding behind the smoker

Through the dining room there's a big backyard — picnic tables, umbrellas, cold beer and the game on. It's the neighborhood's living room from spring through football season.

  • Football Sundays get rowdy — this is Chiefs country, with shrines to Mahomes and Gonzalez inside
  • Craft beer on tap and in cans, plus 16 oz cocktails — rye old fashioneds and raspberry margaritas
  • Room for the whole crew — long tables built for trays and pitchers

The story

Kansas City smoke, Queens address

Pitmaster Josh Bowen learned the trade at Hill Country before opening his own Kansas City-style smokehouse in Long Island City — and New York noticed fast. The original John Brown Smokehouse took Village Voice Best BBQ 2012 and its brisket earned Bowen the “Brisket King of NYC” crown.

When the pandemic forced the Smokehouse to close, Bowen brought the concept back a few blocks away as John Brown BBQ at 27-20 40th Ave — same Kansas City playbook, a brand-new smoker, and a backyard made for long afternoons. The menu reads like KC itself: burnt ends, rib tips, dry-rubbed ribs — plus one New York curveball, pastrami cured and smoked in-house.

No reservations, no white tablecloths. Order at the counter, grab a tray, find a table out back.
